evals.prompt: Define mobile responsive UX for dashboards in 2-3 sentences. Explain why it is more than shrinking the desktop dashboard.
expected_elements: Defines it as redesigning dashboard/operational workflows for small screens, coarse touch, one-handed reach, and quick-glance tasks
States mobile is a different task shape, not the same desktop table or sidebar compressed into a narrow viewport
Names the pocket-control-surface idea: the few readings and actions that matter, within reach
Does NOT define the skill as CSS breakpoints alone

evals.prompt: Name the primitives in the mental model for this skill and explain how they fit together in a mobile dashboard.
expected_elements: Names at least five primitives: reach, target size, glanceable hierarchy, progressive disclosure, touch gestures with visible alternatives, mobile-appropriate inputs, recovery from interrupted use
Connects the primitives to concrete patterns (bottom nav, bottom sheet, card display, 2-up KPIs, pull-to-refresh)
Frames the phone as a control surface for status-check plus one short action
Does NOT treat mobile as a visual scale-down only

evals.prompt: On mobile, what is the trade-off between showing data density and serving the mobile user's task, and how should an agent resolve it for a dashboard?
expected_elements: Desktop optimizes for comparison/filtering/export density; mobile optimizes for a quick health check and one short action
Resolve by progressive disclosure: headline KPIs and a card summary first, detail on tap, full exploration deferred to desktop
A 375px screen cannot and should not show an 8-column table
Density is sacrificed deliberately in favor of glanceability and reach, not by accident

evals.prompt: A desktop dashboard has a sidebar, an 8-column orders table, hover-only row actions, and a complex filter modal. Apply this skill to propose the mobile redesign.
expected_elements: Replace the sidebar with 3-5 bottom-navigation destinations (or a More pattern)
Transform the 8-column table into order cards with 3-4 priority fields each, no horizontal scroll
Give hover-only row actions a visible tap alternative (swipe with a button counterpart)
Move filtering into a bottom sheet rather than a desktop modal
Does NOT keep the 8-column table with horizontal scroll as the primary mobile experience

evals.prompt: What touch-target and thumb-zone rules should an agent enforce when placing controls on a mobile dashboard, and how are they implemented for a small icon?
expected_elements: Recurring interactive controls get at least a 44 x 44 CSS px hit area (mobile ergonomic floor), above WCAG 2.2 AA's 24 x 24 CSS px minimum
A small icon (e.g. 24px) extends its tap area with padding rather than enlarging the glyph
Primary actions go in the bottom 50% (natural thumb zone); rarely-used actions go top/menu
Bottom navigation lives in the natural zone and stays visible

evals.prompt: A teammate asks the mobile-responsive-ux skill to run a full WCAG accessibility audit (ARIA labels, keyboard order, screen-reader behavior) and to define the global responsive grid tracks across all breakpoints. Is that in scope? Why or why not?
expected_elements: WCAG audit breadth (ARIA, keyboard, screen reader, contrast, audit mechanics) is a11y's territory, not this skill's
Global responsive grid tracks across all breakpoints belong to layout-composition
This skill owns mobile-specific touch ergonomics and applies a target-size floor, but defers the compliance audit and cross-breakpoint structure
Correctly redirects rather than over-owning a11y auditing or token/grid architecture

evals.prompt: A stakeholder says 'responsive just means the same dashboard made narrower — add a horizontal scrollbar to the wide table and we're done.' Correct the mental model.
expected_elements: Responsive is not the same screen narrower — the task shape, density, navigation, input, and recovery paths change for touch and interruption
Horizontal-scroll tables are an anti-pattern: most users do not discover scrollable content; use card layouts instead
The mobile job is a health check plus one short action, not full desktop analysis
Moving a CTA to the top of the screen or compressing density is a misread of the mobile use case, not a layout detail

evals.prompt: What would you check to verify a mobile dashboard redesign was implemented correctly?
expected_elements: All interactive elements are at least 44 x 44 CSS px and primary actions sit in the bottom 50%
Data tables are replaced with card layouts below 640px (no horizontal table scroll)
Bottom navigation has at most 5 items with icon + label; no hover-only interactions remain
KPI cards use a 2-up layout; pull-to-refresh exists for data lists
Verified on a real device, not just a DevTools resize
